title: coverage-manifest-v1
description: Durable record of ONE acquisition or reconciliation operation and the DECLARED COVERAGE it asserts for a dataset. This is the reconstructible source of catalog.partitions.ts_start / ts_end, which partition-manifest-v1 does not carry: first_exchange_ts / last_exchange_ts are OBSERVED EVENT BOUNDS and can never produce declared coverage. The document is keyed to the natural dataset identity rather than to a file, because coverage is asserted over intervals: an interval may contain zero events, an interval may be known-uncovered while no partition exists for it, and coverage may be revised by a later repair without the sealed content changing. Acquisition INTENT and certified coverage are separate concepts: 'acquisition' records what the operation set out to obtain, 'assertions' records what it may legitimately declare. Supersession is wholesale, at document level. NO absolute paths. NOTHING strategic or derived.

layer.description: Layer of the owning dataset. Part of the natural identity.

dataset_kind.description: Nature of the data. Part of the natural identity.

venue.description: Venue of the owning dataset. Mandatory and non-null in every layer, as in partition-manifest-v1.

instrument.description: Instrument of the owning dataset. Carries the NATIVE venue value: case and punctuation are not normalized.

feature_set_slug.description: Required if and only if layer is 'features'.

feature_set_version.description: Required if and only if layer is 'features'.

record_schema_id.description: Record schema, e.g. 'trade-v1'. Part of the natural dataset identity.

coverage_id.description: Stable identity of THIS coverage manifest, unique within the dataset. It is what 'supersedes' points at, so it must never be reused after a revision.

supersedes.description: coverage_id of the document this one replaces, or null. Supersession is WHOLESALE: the superseded document contributes nothing afterwards, so this document must RESTATE every interval it still holds true. Its acquisition interval must therefore contain the superseded document's acquisition interval, otherwise a narrow repair would silently drop coverage outside its own window. The semantic validator enforces that containment.

created_at.description: Instant at which this coverage manifest was written.

acquisition.description: What the operation SET OUT to obtain, and under which source semantics. Requesting, downloading or subscribing to an interval does not certify that interval: this block is intent, 'assertions' is what may be declared. The union of the assertions must lie inside this interval.

basis.description: How the operation acquired, or attempted to acquire, the interval. 'source_archive': a published archive or dump. 'api_request': a finite request/pagination sequence against a provider API. 'source_extract': a deterministic extraction over an already-held local source, such as SQL over a legacy database. 'source_session': one bounded connected session of a source. 'live_stream': a closed segment of persistent live collection. 'backfill': finite acquisition intended to repair a known gap. 'reconciliation': no new acquisition, a restatement that reconciles evidence already held.

intent_start.description: Start of the intended acquisition interval, inclusive. Same microsecond ceiling as the assertion boundaries it must contain — see coverage_assertion.start.

intent_end.description: End of the intended acquisition interval, EXCLUSIVE. Half-open [intent_start, intent_end), the same convention DataGateway uses. A persistent live collector emits one document per CLOSED segment, so the segment bounds are known when the document is written. Same microsecond ceiling as coverage_assertion.end.

source_semantics.description: Versioned identity of the SOURCE-SPECIFIC semantics this operation relied on, for example 'bybit-public-trades-sqlite-v1'. It names what the facts of that source mean; it is not the canonical record schema. Versioned so that a later reinterpretation of the same source becomes a distinct identity instead of silently reinterpreting past evidence.

mapping.description: Versioned identity of the mapping applied from those source facts to canonical declared coverage, for example 'bybit-sqlite-day-extract-v1'. Venue-specific coverage reasoning lives behind this identity; the canonical representation below stays venue-independent.

assertions.description: What the operation may legitimately declare, interval by interval. Not derived from event timestamps, not derived from partition_key.

producer.description: Process that performed this operation, for example 'bybit-collector'.

code_ref.description: EXACT Git revision that performed this operation. Same role as partition-manifest-v1.code_ref: implementation identity, not semantic identity.

allOf.description: layer 'features' <-> feature-set definition identity. Mirrors partition-manifest-v1.

coverage_assertion.description: One declared interval and the evidence supporting it.

assertion_id.description: Stable identity of THIS assertion. Array position is NOT identity: reordering, inserting or removing a sibling assertion must not change what an existing assertion_id refers to. Unique within this one coverage-manifest document only — it is not a cross-document or global identifier, and carries no runtime, path or catalog UUID.

start.description: Start of the declared interval, inclusive. Coverage boundaries are capped at MICROSECOND precision — the current PostgreSQL catalog.partitions.ts_start/ts_end columns are timestamptz, which round-trips microseconds exactly and would silently truncate a finer value. Event timestamps (trade-v1 exchange_ts/receive_ts, partition-manifest-v1 first/last_exchange_ts) are unaffected and keep their existing nanosecond-capable precision — this ceiling applies only to declared coverage boundaries.

end.description: End of the declared interval, EXCLUSIVE. Half-open [start, end), so adjacency where A.end == B.start is contiguous without overlap. A degenerate start == end is rejected by the semantic validator: an empty declaration asserts nothing. Same microsecond ceiling as `start`.

status.description: 'complete': the canonical records for this interval are materialized and the evidence supports that nothing is missing; ZERO events is a legitimate complete interval. 'uncertain': the producer lacks sufficient evidence either way. 'known_gap': the producer positively knows the interval is not covered, either because it was not observing (transport interruption) or because source events are known to be missing (sequence discontinuity); those two are distinguished by the evidence kind, not by a fourth status. ONLY 'complete' contributes to catalog.partitions.ts_start / ts_end.

partitions.description: Natural partition identities this assertion attributes coverage to. A 'complete' assertion attributes to EXACTLY ONE partition, so per-partition declared coverage is determined without circularity: an archive spanning three partitions emits three complete assertions inside one document, rather than one assertion naming three partitions. 'uncertain' and 'known_gap' may name zero partitions, which is how a gap stays representable when nothing was ever materialized for it.

evidence.description: Source-specific facts supporting the status. At least one. The venue-specific reasoning behind them is named by acquisition.source_semantics and acquisition.mapping.

allOf.description: A complete interval must be materialized somewhere, in exactly one partition. Zero events still requires a zero-row partition to exist, otherwise DataGateway would hold coverage with nothing to read.

natural_partition_ref.description: Natural partition identity within this dataset: partition_key plus revision. NOT the catalog partition UUID, which is a runtime locator and does not survive a catalog rebuild.

partition_key.description: Same grammar frozen in partition-manifest-v1. It identifies the partition; it does NOT define the declared interval.

kind.description: Venue-independent classification of the supporting fact. 'archive_completeness': a published archive was retrieved and verified whole. 'pagination_complete': a finite request sequence reached its documented terminal condition. 'deterministic_source_extract': a deterministic extraction read an already-held local source exhaustively over the interval; this proves the LOCAL source was read completely, never that the local source holds everything the venue originally published. 'connection_continuity': the source connection stayed established across the interval. 'transport_interruption': the connection was lost and observation stopped. 'sequence_continuity': a native source sequence was contiguous across the interval. 'sequence_discontinuity': a native source sequence skipped values, so source events are known to be missing. 'reconciliation': a later authoritative operation confirmed or repaired the interval. This vocabulary is deliberately MINIMAL and covers only the cases the frozen semantics require. L2 snapshot validity and L3/MBO reconstruction continuity are NOT frozen here; adding a kind is additive contract evolution under ADR-0018.

detail.description: Human- and audit-readable specifics of this fact: the archive name, the terminal pagination cursor, the observed sequence values, the reconnect instants. Free text on purpose, because freezing a per-kind payload now would freeze future L1/L2/L3 evidence formats.

utc_timestamp.description: UTC instant in RFC 3339, mandatory 'Z' suffix, up to 9 decimal digits. Used only for `created_at`, document bookkeeping metadata that never becomes a catalog coverage boundary and does not carry the microsecond ceiling below. ORDERING AND COMPARISON always use the PARSED temporal value, never the string.

coverage_timestamp.description: UTC instant in RFC 3339, mandatory 'Z' suffix, AT MOST 6 decimal digits. Used for every value that becomes or bounds a declared coverage boundary (acquisition.intent_start/intent_end, coverage_assertion.start/end) so that catalog.partitions.ts_start/ts_end, PostgreSQL timestamptz columns with microsecond resolution, can hold every accepted value exactly. This is a v1 policy ceiling on the DECLARED interval, not a redefinition of trade-v1 or partition-manifest-v1 event-timestamp precision, which remain nanosecond-capable and untouched. ORDERING AND COMPARISON always use the PARSED temporal value, never the string.

canonical_identifier.description: Path-safe canonical identifier: lowercase, alphanumeric components separated by a single '.', '_' or '-'.

versioned_identifier.description: A canonical identifier that MUST carry an explicit '-v<N>' suffix, so that 'versioned source semantics' is a mechanical property rather than an intention.
